Method of Attack: GoldMax: Go-based malware used as a command-and-control backdoor for hiding malicious activity and evading detection, with a decoy network traffic generator for concealing malicious network traffic with seemingly benign traffic
Sibot: VBScript-based malware used for maintaining persistence and downloading additional malware payloads using a second-stage script
GoldFinder: Go-based malware most likely used as a custom HTTP tracer tool for detecting servers and redirectors like network security devices between the infected devices and C2 server
Sunshuttle: second-stage backdoor malware linked to SolarWinds hackers, capable of hiding C2 traffic
Impacted Systems: networks targeted by SolarWinds supply-chain attack
Attack Vector: lateral movement with TEARDROP and hands-on-keyboard actions
Date of Discovery: 2020 (disclosed August-September 2020 activity, believed dropped as early as June 2020)
Indicators of Compromise: Shared C2 domain between Sunshuttle and GoldMax
